title: Fix chained expression indentation
description:
Method chains and null coalesce operators on continuation lines are not indented. They should be indented relative to the receiver expression.

Expected (pkl format):
```
result =
  items
    .filter((x) -> x > 0)
    .map((x) -> x * 2)
    .toList()

value =
  a
    ?? b
    ?? c
```

Actual (pkl-ts-mode):
```
result =
  items
.filter((x) -> x > 0)
.map((x) -> x * 2)
.toList()

value =
  a
?? b
?? c
```

Chained method calls (qualifiedAccessExpr) and binary operators like `??` (nullCoalesceExpr) on continuation lines need indentation rules. The pattern is: indent continuation lines 2 extra spaces relative to the receiver/left operand.

title: Fix nested if expression indentation
description:
When an `if` expression is nested inside the consequent of another `if` expression, the inner `if` is not indented correctly.

Expected (pkl format):
```
result =
  if (a > 0)
    if (b > 0)
      "both positive"
    else
      "b not positive"
  else
    "a not positive"
```

Actual (pkl-ts-mode):
```
result =
  if (a > 0)
  if (b > 0)
    "both positive"
  else
    "b not positive"
  else
    "a not positive"
```

The inner `if` should be indented 4 spaces (one level deeper than the outer `if`), but it is only indented 2 spaces (same level as the outer `if`). This is because the inner `ifExpr` is a direct child of the outer `ifExpr`, and the current `ifExpr` indent rule excludes `if` and `else` keywords from additional indentation. The inner `if` keyword needs to be recognized as a child of the outer `ifExpr` consequent position, not as the keyword of the outer `ifExpr`.

title: Fix block comment indentation
description:
Block comment continuation lines are not indented correctly. The `*` characters lose their alignment.

Expected (pkl format):
```
/*
 * This is a block comment
 * with multiple lines
 */
```

Actual (pkl-ts-mode):
```
/*
* This is a block comment
  * with multiple lines
    */
```

The `prev-adaptive-prefix` anchor is not producing the correct indentation for block comment continuation lines.
close_reason: Replaced prev-adaptive-prefix anchor with parent-bol 1 for blockComment indentation rule

title: Fix let expression indentation
description:
Subsequent `let` bindings and the body expression in a let chain are not indented correctly. Only the first `let` gets indented.

Expected (pkl format):
```
result =
  let (x = 42)
  let (y = x + 1)
    x + y
```

Actual (pkl-ts-mode):
```
result =
  let (x = 42)
let (y = x + 1)
x + y
```

The tree-sitter structure for let expressions is nested: the outer `letExpr` contains a `let` keyword, a binding, and a body expression. When the body is another `letExpr`, it should be aligned with the outer `let`. The final body expression should be indented one level deeper than the `let` keywords.

title: Fix multiline string indentation on continuation lines
description:
When a multiline string literal (`"""`) starts on a continuation line (after `=`), the string body and closing `"""` are over-indented.

Expected (pkl format):
```
message =
  """
  Hello,
    World!
  """
```

Actual (pkl-ts-mode):
```
message =
  """
    Hello,
    World!
    """
```

The opening `"""` is correctly indented to column 2, but the string body lines and closing `"""` get an extra 2 spaces of indentation. This happens because the `mlStringLiteralExpr` rule adds `pkl-ts-mode-indent-offset` relative to `parent-bol`, but when the `"""` itself is on a continuation line (already indented by the `classProperty` rule), the string contents get double-indented.

The existing multiline string test passes because in that test the `"""` is on the same line as the `=`, so there is no continuation-line indentation conflict.
